module purpose: neorv32_cpu_alu compares rs1_i and rs2_i, selects operands for arithmetic and logical ALU operations, and drives compare flags, an adder/subtractor result, and the selected execution result on its outputs. It also aggregates coprocessor results and valid signals, qualifies FPU and CFU CSR accesses, returns coprocessor CSR read data, and tracks custom-function-unit activity.

use-case flows.value: comparison outcome between rs1_i and rs2_i, with signed/unsigned handling, driven to cmp_o and forwarded to compare-using coprocessors
operand-selected add/subtract result driven on add_o
selected non-coprocessor ALU result on res_o (zero, add, set-less-than, move, xor, or, and)
aggregated coprocessor result formed from coprocessor result channels and selected onto res_o for alu_op_cp_c
coprocessor completion indication on done_o from the cp_valid lines
qualified FPU CSR write request and FPU CSR read gating
qualified CFU CSR write request and CFU CSR read gating
custom-function-unit request activation and in-progress tracking
selected FPU or CFU CSR read data returned on csr_o
CFU in-progress state cleared and local captured CFU result forced to zero when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Comparison outcome for rs1_i and rs2_i
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 97-101 form signed/unsigned compare operands and compute equality and less-than bits in cmp; line 102 exports that decision on cmp_o, and lines 230 and 263 deliver it to the bitmanip and FPU coprocessors. Integrity is established because those consumers must receive exactly the comparison bits defined by these statements; availability is established because cmp and cmp_o are continuously driven from the current inputs.

Lines 107 and 108 choose opa and opb, lines 113 and 114 extend them according to ctrl_i.alu_unsigned, and lines 116-117 perform subtraction or addition before line 119 drives add_o. Integrity is established because add_o and the arithmetic branches of res_o depend on this exact relation between the selected operands; availability is established because add_o is continuously driven from addsub_res.

The alu_core process always assigns res_o, with ctrl_i.alu_op selecting zero, add, set-less-than, move, xor, or, and at lines 127-136. Integrity is established because the external consumer of res_o must receive the value chosen by that operation selector and the branch-specific computations at lines 129 and 131-135; availability is established because the process always drives res_o, including default zero assignments at lines 126, 128, and 136.

Coprocessor subunits drive cp_result at lines 176, 199, 235, 268, 372, and 406, while the CFU path captures cfu_res into cp_result(4) at line 335 and forces zero otherwise at line 337. Line 151 ORs the cp_result channels into cp_res, and line 130 places cp_res onto res_o for alu_op_cp_c. Integrity is established because the consumer of res_o must receive exactly the coprocessor result selected by this path; availability is conditional on enabled coprocessor builds and, for the CFU slot, on the done/active condition at lines 334-335.

Line 147 reports done_o as the OR of all cp_valid bits. Those validity channels come from coprocessor valid_o outputs at lines 177, 200, 236, 269, 373, and 407, plus the local CFU-valid decision at line 343. Integrity is established because done_o is the module's completion report for these coprocessor paths; availability is established because done_o is continuously driven from the current valid vector.

When RISCV_ISA_Zfinx is enabled, line 275 gates fpu_csr_rd onto csr_rdata_fpu under the address-match decision from line 273; when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu is enabled, line 320 gates cfu_csr_rd onto csr_rdata_cfu under the address-match decision from line 318. Line 155 ORs both qualified readback buses into csr_o, while disabled builds force zeros at lines 282 and 350. Integrity is established because csr_o must return the addressed enabled coprocessor CSR data defined by these statements; availability is established only under the matching decode and enabled generic conditions.

Under RISCV_ISA_Zfinx, line 273 decodes ctrl_i.csr_addr into fpu_csr_en and line 274 combines that decode with ctrl_i.csr_we to form fpu_csr_we, which is delivered to the FPU coprocessor at line 258. When the feature is not built, lines 280-281 force both decisions to zero. Integrity is established because the FPU consumer must receive a write-enable only for addressed FPU CSR writes defined by this logic; availability is established only in enabled builds and when the decode and write-enable conditions hold.

Under RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu, line 318 decodes ctrl_i.csr_addr into cfu_csr_en and line 319 combines that decode with ctrl_i.csr_we to form cfu_csr_we, which is delivered to the CFU coprocessor at line 301. When the feature is not built, lines 348-349 force both decisions to zero. Integrity is established because the CFU consumer must receive a write-enable only for addressed CFU CSR writes defined by this logic; availability is established only in enabled builds and when the decode and write-enable conditions hold.

When RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu is enabled, ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu starts the CFU at line 298, lines 329-332 update cfu_busy so the request remains pending until cfu_done or ctrl_i.cpu_trap, and line 342 computes cfu_active from the current request or busy state. Lines 334-343 then use that state to qualify returned result and valid information. Reset clears the state at lines 325-326, and disabled builds force zero at lines 351-352. Integrity is established because this state determines whether the CFU remains active and whether returned data/valid belong to a pending request; availability is established under the explicit start, done, trap, and reset conditions visible in the RTL.
